2538	### Source-number mapping
2539	
2540	The authoritative BK7258 `icu_map.h` contains 64 entries and maps every SDK
2541	source one-to-one:
2542	
2543	```text
2544	SDK source 0..63 -> external NVIC line 0..63
2545	                 -> NuttX logical IRQ 16..79
2546	```

2548	The linked `icu_int_map_table` bytes independently confirm each record has
2549	`src == int_bit` from 0 through 63. Anchors remain TIMER=3, TIMER1=13,
2550	UART1=15, ETH=48, SCALE0=49, MAILBOX=63.

2553	
2554	The CP CM33 implementation performs:
2555	
2556	- register: validate `src < 64`, unregister/replace the old callback, install the
2557	  new `void (*)(void)` callback, enable the NVIC line, then apply mapped default
2558	  priority 6;
2559	- unregister: validate `src < 64`, disable the NVIC line, clear its callback;
2560	- set-priority: apply the caller's CMSIS priority value;
2561	- the supplied `arg` is ignored;
2562	- callbacks run in ISR context and take no arguments.

2564	CMSIS uses `__NVIC_PRIO_BITS=3`; SDK priority 6 is encoded in the hardware byte
2565	as `6 << 5 == 0xc0`. NuttX `up_prioritize_irq()` accepts an already encoded
2566	priority byte, so the bridge must translate SDK priorities before calling it.

2570	Defining only `bk_int_isr_register()` is not robust: any later unresolved
2571	reference to `bk_int_isr_unregister`, `bk_int_set_priority`, `interrupt_init`, or
2572	`interrupt_deinit` could extract the whole original archive object and create a
2573	strong-symbol collision. The dedicated overlay bridge therefore needs to own
2574	all five callable symbols from the CM33 path. Archive-wide undefined-symbol
2575	inspection found no external consumer of `icu_int_map_table`, so the table need
2576	not be reproduced; direct `src + 16` mapping is sufficient and keeps the
2577	original object unextracted.

19	config ARCH_CHIP_BK7258
20		bool "Beken BK7258 (T5-AI tri-core Cortex-M33)"
21		depends on ARCH_CHIP_CUSTOM
22		select ARCH_CORTEXM33
23		select ARCH_HAVE_FPU
24		select ARCH_HAVE_CUSTOM_VECTORS
25		select ARCH_RAMVECTORS
26		select ARCH_HAVE_MPU
27		select MTD if BK7258_FLASH_MTD
28		---help---
29			Beken BK7258 SoC as shipped on the T5-AI board: tri-core
30			Cortex-M33.  This Stage N1 port targets a single app core that
31			the on-board Tier-1 bootloader (board/bk7258_t5ai/bootloader)
32			jumps to at logical flash address 0x02010000 after validating
33			the app magic "BK7236\0\0" at image offset 0x100.
34	
35			The chip provides its own Cortex-M vector table (selected via
36			ARCH_HAVE_CUSTOM_VECTORS) so that the BK7236 app magic can be
37			placed at vector slot 64/65 (image offset 0x100), exactly where
38			the bootloader looks for it.
39	
40	config BK7258_FLASH_MTD
41		bool "BK7258 on-chip flash data-partition MTD"
42		default n
43		depends on ARCH_CHIP_BK7258
44		select MTD
45		---help---
46			Expose the 1 MiB data partition (logical 0x00100000..0x001FFFFF)
47			as a NuttX MTD instance.  read/erase/bwrite use the
48			option-A SR0 block-protect policy (cleared around each op,
49			restored afterwards).  No /dev node or filesystem is mounted
50			by this driver; a filesystem mount requires separate
51			authorisation (see BK7258_FLASH_LITTLEFS).
52	
53	config BK7258_FLASH_LITTLEFS
54		bool "BK7258 data-partition LittleFS (auto-format + mount)"
55		default n
56		depends on BK7258_FLASH_MTD
57		select FS_LITTLEFS
58		---help---
59			Register /dev/mtdblock0 (ftl) over the data-partition MTD and mount
60			LittleFS at /data with the "autoformat" option (formats on first
61			boot only).  Also runs a probe-file persistence check.
62			Destructive on the data partition; enable only when authorised.
63	
64	config BK7258_CLOCK_320M
65		bool "BK7258 deterministic 320 MHz CPU0 clock bring-up"
66		default n
67		depends on ARCH_CHIP_BK7258
68		select BK7258_DVFS
69		---help---
70			Deterministically bring the CPU0 core clock to the 320 MHz tier
71			(DPLL /1.5, the highest board-verified operating point; CPU0
72			effective 160 MHz on this single-core port -- see BK7258_DVFS)
73			at boot.  The bootloader enables + calibrates the DPLL at the SDK
74			default analog state; this option makes the app step the core up
75			to the 320 MHz runtime tier via bk7258_dvfs_set_freq().  480 MHz
76			direct is SDK-rejected and not attempted.
77	
78	config BK7258_CLOCK_320M_PROBE
79		bool "BK7258 320 MHz bring-up verification probe (uart evidence line)"
80		default n
81		depends on BK7258_CLOCK_320M
82		---help---
83			Re-add a one-shot freestanding UART evidence line after the 320 MHz
84			bring-up showing M1/ANA_REG5/ANA_REG9 readback, for one
85			verification build.  Disable after board-verify.
86	
87	config BK7258_DVFS
88		bool "BK7258 runtime CPU-frequency switching (DVFS lower half)"
89		default n
90		depends on ARCH_CHIP_BK7258
91		---help---
92			Provide bk7258_dvfs_set_freq(int tier) -- a standalone NuttX
93			overlay DVFS lower half that mirrors the Armino SDK runtime
94			sys_drv_switch_cpu_bus_freq / sys_hal_switch_cpu_bus_freq path
95			(lift VDDD/VDDIG one tier at a time per the SDK operating-point
96			table, then switch the core mux, then recompute the SysTick
97			reload).  This is NOT the NuttX PM state machine: it follows the
98			lc823450 DVFS precedent of a single chip-local set_freq() with no
99			governor/HPWORK dependency.  Boot-time bring-up under
100			BK7258_CLOCK_320M selects this; runtime switching via /proc/dvfs
101			is available under BK7258_DVFS_PROCFS.
102	
103	config BK7258_DVFS_PROCFS
104		bool "BK7258 /proc/dvfs runtime DVFS control"
105		default n
106		depends on BK7258_DVFS
107		select FS_PROCFS
108		select FS_PROCFS_REGISTER
109		---help---
110			Register /proc/dvfs so the current CPU frequency tier can be
111			queried (`cat /proc/dvfs`) and stepped at runtime
112			(`echo "cur_freq 80" > /proc/dvfs`), exercising the full DVFS
113			lower half from userspace.  Requires FS_PROCFS +
114			FS_PROCFS_REGISTER (both selected here) for the procfs_register
115			run-time registration API.
116	
117	config BK7258_WDT
118		bool "BK7258 APB watchdog (WDT) lower-half driver"
119		default y
120		depends on ARCH_CHIP_BK7258
121		select WATCHDOG
122		---help---
123			Register /dev/watchdog0 backed by the BK7258 APB hardware
124			watchdog.  Mirrors the Armino SDK WDT BSP
125			(bk_wdt_driver_init / bk_wdt_start / bk_wdt_feed path).
126			The bootloader arms the WDT during cold-init; this driver
127			takes over after boot and feeds it via the NuttX watchdog
128			upper-half automonitor (CONFIG_WATCHDOG_AUTOMONITOR).
129			Default timeout 8 s (period=8000), matching the bootloader.
130	
131	config BK7258_SDK_IRQ_BRIDGE
132		bool "Beken SDK CPU0 interrupt bridge"
133		default n
134		depends on ARCH_CHIP_BK7258
135		select ARCH_IRQPRIO
136		---help---
137			Route the Beken SDK interrupt registration APIs through the NuttX
138			IRQ subsystem on CPU0.  SDK sources 0..63 map one-to-one to
139			NuttX logical IRQs 16..79.  This option requires the A1 80-slot
140			RAM-vector table and does not provide AP/CPU1/CPU2 SMP support.

7	 *
8	 * Memory map (reverse-engineered on board; the app partition size follows
9	 * the armino SDK partition table for BK7258):
10	 *
11	 *   FLASH : 0x02010000 .. 0x020FFFFF  (1 MiB logical/XIP window)
12	 *           The on-flash primary_cp_app partition is 1360 KiB (see the
13	 *           armino BK7258 partition CSVs), so a 1 MiB link window sits
14	 *           comfortably inside it.  (Stage N1 used a 64 KiB placeholder
15	 *           because the N1 image was tiny; the full NuttX kernel + NSH is
16	 *           ~70 KiB and would not fit in 64 KiB.)  The Tier-1 bootloader
17	 *           jumps the app Reset entry here after validating the BK7236
18	 *           magic.
19	 *   RAM   : 0x28000000 .. 0x2809FFFF  (640 KiB SRAM)
20	 *   MSP   : 0x2809FFFC  (top of usable SRAM, also stored in vector slot 0)
21	 *
22	 * The .vectors section (80 entries, 0x140 bytes from bk7258_vectors.c) is
23	 * KEEP-pinned first so that:
24	 *   - file offset 0x000 == slot [0] == initial MSP (0x2809FFFC)
25	 *   - file offset 0x004 == slot [1] == __start (Thumb entry)
26	 *   - file offset 0x100 == slot [64] == app magic "BK72"
27	 *   - file offset 0x104 == slot [65] == app magic "36\0\0"
28	 *   - file offset 0x108 == slot [66] == first upper external IRQ
29	 *   - file offset 0x13c == slot [79] == last upper external IRQ
30	 ****************************************************************************/
31	
32	/* The linker script is preprocessed to .tmp before being passed to ld;
33	 * include the build config so CONFIG_ARCH_INTERRUPTSTACK (used in
34	 * .irq_stack below) and any other CONFIG_* values are substituted.
35	 */
36	
37	#include <nuttx/config.h>
38	
39	OUTPUT_ARCH("arm")
40	EXTERN(_vectors)
41	ENTRY(__start)
42	
43	MEMORY
44	{
45	    FLASH (rx)  : ORIGIN = 0x02010000, LENGTH = 0x100000
46	    RAM   (rwx) : ORIGIN = 0x28000000, LENGTH = 0xA0000
47	}
48	
49	/* Initial stack pointer (top of SRAM).  Also stored in vector slot 0. */
50	
51	_estack = 0x2809fffc;
52	
53	SECTIONS
54	{
55	    /* Vector table FIRST, pinned at 0x02010000.  KEEP() prevents the
56	     * linker from GC'ing it; . = ORIGIN(FLASH) pins the address.
57	     */
58	    . = ORIGIN(FLASH);
59	    .vectors : ALIGN(4)
60	    {
61	        KEEP(*(.vectors))
62	        . = ALIGN(4);
63	    } > FLASH
64	
65	    /* Permanent A1 linker gates for .vectors section.
66	     * _vectors must be pinned at flash origin; size must be 0x140 (80 slots).
67	     */
68	
69	    ASSERT(_vectors == ORIGIN(FLASH),
70	           "ERROR: _vectors must be at ORIGIN(FLASH) = 0x02010000 (A1 gate)")
71	    ASSERT(SIZEOF(.vectors) == 0x140,
72	           "ERROR: .vectors must be 0x140 bytes (80 entries, A1 gate)")
73	
74	    /* Code + read-only data (XIP-readable in flash). */
75	    .text : ALIGN(4)
76	    {
77	        _stext = ABSOLUTE(.);
78	        *(.text .text.*)
79	        *(.fixup)
80	        *(.gnu.warning)
81	        *(.rodata .rodata.*)
82	        *(.gnu.linkonce.t.*)
83	        *(.glue_7)
84	        *(.glue_7t)
85	        *(.gcc_except_table)
86	        *(.gnu.linkonce.r.*)
87	        . = ALIGN(4);
88	        _etext = ABSOLUTE(.);
89	    } > FLASH
90	
91	    /* Constructors / destructors (NuttX init_section convention). */
92	    .init_section : ALIGN(4)
93	    {
94	        _sinit = ABSOLUTE(.);
95	        KEEP(*(SORT_BY_INIT_PRIORITY(.init_array.*) SORT_BY_INIT_PRIORITY(.ctors.*)))
96	        KEEP(*(.init_array EXCLUDE_FILE(*crtbegin.o *crtbegin?.o *crtend.o *crtend?.o) .ctors))
97	        _einit = ABSOLUTE(.);
98	    } > FLASH
99	
100	    /* ARM exception unwinding tables -- keep them out of the way. */

## 2026-07-23 -- Stage B archive-selection fix implemented (unrebuilt)

### Root cause

The final ARM link places all standard NuttX archives (`LDLIBS`, including
`libarch.a`) and SDK `EXTRA_LIBS` inside one linker group. Before any SDK driver
creates an unresolved `bk_int_isr_register` reference, the first `libarch.a` scan
has no reason to extract `bk7258_sdk_irq.o`. Later in the same group,
`libdriver.a(timer_driver.c.obj)` creates the reference and the same SDK archive
immediately satisfies it with `interrupt_base.c.obj`. A subsequent group rescan
cannot replace an already resolved strong definition.

### Team-overlay fix

Added a configuration-gated linker-script root:

```ld
#ifdef CONFIG_BK7258_SDK_IRQ_BRIDGE
EXTERN(bk_int_isr_register)
#endif
```

The linker script is already preprocessed with `<nuttx/config.h>`. Therefore this
creates the unresolved bridge symbol before the archive group is scanned, causing
the earlier NuttX `libarch.a` to extract `bk7258_sdk_irq.o`. Extracting that one
member also supplies unregister, set-priority, init, and deinit, so the later SDK
`interrupt_base.c.obj` should remain unextracted. This avoids whole-archiving
`libarch.a`, direct object-path duplication, or any official-tree/SDK edit.

The Stage B verifier now has source gate `S10`, requiring the conditional linker
root and `EXTERN(bk_int_isr_register)` declaration.

### Status and boundary

Fix is `static-only` / unrebuilt. No claim of link ownership is made until a fresh
build and verifier run are GREEN. No flash, board test, commit, or push occurred.

### Next single minimal action

Run source syntax/whitespace checks, then a fresh distclean/build and the same
post-link verifier. If ownership turns GREEN, run the preserved A1 vector/magic /
partition gates before preparing the user-only timer board test.

## 2026-07-23 -- Focused review finds per-source default-priority defect

### Finding F1 (`Important`)

The authoritative BK7258 `ICU_DEV_MAP` is one-to-one for source/line numbers, but
its default priority is not uniform:

```text
sources 0..26, 28..63: IQR_PRI_DEFAULT = 6 -> raw 0xc0
source 27 (INT_SRC_LCD): explicit priority 0 -> raw 0x00
```

The current bridge instead uses `BK7258_SDK_IRQ_DEFAULT_PRIORITY` (`6`) for every
source. Registering `INT_SRC_LCD` would therefore change the SDK-defined default
from logical priority 0 to 6. This violates the required mapped-default lifecycle
semantics even though archive ownership and all current verifier gates are GREEN.

The earlier statement that all 64 sources use default priority 6 is retracted.
The existing verifier also has a coverage gap: it checks the register call path
but not the per-source mapped default or `bk_int_set_priority()` call path.

### Status

Overall Stage B returns to `blocked` pending this semantic correction and verifier
hardening. The link-order fix and A1 invariant results remain valid evidence, but
the current artifact must not be board-tested. No flash, commit, or push occurred.

### Next single minimal action

Implement a pinned `INT_SRC_LCD == 27` priority exception (0; all other sources 6),
harden the verifier for mapped defaults, generated config, and the custom-priority
call path, then rebuild and rerun all Stage B/A1 gates.

319	## 2026-07-21 — Tri-core SMP/AMP design boundary
320	
321	The current verified port runs one NuttX instance on CPU0; therefore the
322	current vector, NVIC, UART and SDK IRQ bridge work is scoped to CPU0. A
323	three-core chip does not by itself mean that the current NuttX configuration
324	is SMP. Other cores running separate SDK firmware would be an AMP arrangement
325	and must retain their own local interrupt handling, with cross-core events
326	using the chip IPC/mailbox path rather than CPU0 `g_irqvector[]`.
327	
328	The CPU0 bridge should nevertheless avoid UP-only assumptions: protect shared
329	registration state with a spinlock rather than only local interrupt masking,
330	separate one-time callback-table initialization from per-core NVIC setup, and
331	make interrupt ownership/routing explicit. It must not silently enable the
332	same peripheral IRQ on multiple cores.
333	
334	A future NuttX SMP port would be a separate architecture milestone requiring
335	secondary-core startup, per-core VTOR/IRQ-stack setup, inter-processor
336	interrupts, scheduler SMP hooks, per-core timer policy, interrupt affinity and
337	cache/coherency validation. The SDK IRQ bridge alone does not provide those
338	facilities and must not be described as tri-core SMP completion.
339	
340	Status: `static-only` design constraint. Preserve room for later per-core
341	routing rather than mixing SMP bring-up into the current UART/WDT recovery
342	stage.

344	## 2026-07-21 — Targeted SDK IRQ and multicore evidence
345	
346	The BK7258 SDK does not use the earlier assumed 48-entry external IRQ model.
347	Targeted source inspection established the following static facts:
348	
349	- `middleware/soc/bk7258/soc/icu_map.h` maps 64 SDK interrupt sources
350	  one-to-one to external NVIC indices 0 through 63. `INT_SRC_MAILBOX` maps to
351	  external IRQ 63.
352	- `middleware/driver/bk7258/interrupt.c` defines handlers for external IRQs
353	  0 through 63. Each fixed vector handler calls `arch_interrupt_get_handler()`
354	  and then invokes the callback stored for that NVIC index.
355	- `middleware/arch/cm33/arch_interrupt.c` owns a local
356	  `s_irq_handler[64]`. Registration stores a callback, sets priority and
357	  enables that local NVIC IRQ; unregistration disables it and clears the
358	  callback. The SDK `bk_int_isr_register()` path ignores its `arg` parameter.
359	- SDK startup sources provide separate CPU0, CPU1 and CPU2 vector tables. The
360	  inspected BK7258 library configuration sets `CONFIG_CPU_CNT=2`, while
361	  optional `CONFIG_SOC_SMP` paths and AMP resource/mailbox code coexist.
362	- Under `CONFIG_SOC_SMP`, mailbox channels are explicitly hard-bound to a
363	  processor through `sys_drv_core_intr_group2_enable()`. AMP resource sharing
364	  uses mailbox IPC and per-CPU ownership/counting.
365	
366	This overturns the previous proposed constants. A complete NuttX logical IRQ
367	space for 64 external IRQs would normally require:
368	
369	```text
370	BK7258_EXTERNAL_IRQS = 64
371	NR_IRQS = 16 + 64 = 80
372	```
373	
374	However, the current bootable NuttX image places mandatory bootloader magic at
375	image offset `0x100`, which is vector slot 64. A contiguous 80-entry runtime
376	vector table would need slots 64 through 79 for external IRQs 48 through 63,
377	so simply changing `NR_IRQS` to 80 would overwrite or conflict with the boot
378	magic layout. The current table only provides external IRQs 0 through 47;
379	UART1 works because it is external IRQ 15.
380	
381	Status: `static-only`, newly identified blocker. The earlier
382	"48 external IRQs / `NR_IRQS=64`" correction is `rejected` and must not be
383	implemented.
384	
385	Next single minimal action: reconcile the vendor boot image/vector layout with
386	its 64-entry runtime IRQ table and determine whether NuttX must keep a minimal
387	boot table at the image origin and switch VTOR after reset to a separate full
388	80-slot runtime table. Do not implement the SDK bridge or change IRQ counts
389	until this layout is proven.

2822	## 2026-07-23 -- Stage B archive-selection fix implemented (unrebuilt)
2823	
2824	### Root cause
2825	
2826	The final ARM link places all standard NuttX archives (`LDLIBS`, including
2827	`libarch.a`) and SDK `EXTRA_LIBS` inside one linker group. Before any SDK driver
2828	creates an unresolved `bk_int_isr_register` reference, the first `libarch.a` scan
2829	has no reason to extract `bk7258_sdk_irq.o`. Later in the same group,
2830	`libdriver.a(timer_driver.c.obj)` creates the reference and the same SDK archive
2831	immediately satisfies it with `interrupt_base.c.obj`. A subsequent group rescan
2832	cannot replace an already resolved strong definition.
2833	
2834	### Team-overlay fix
2835	
2836	Added a configuration-gated linker-script root:
2837	
2838	```ld
2839	#ifdef CONFIG_BK7258_SDK_IRQ_BRIDGE
2840	EXTERN(bk_int_isr_register)
2841	#endif
2842	```
2843	
2844	The linker script is already preprocessed with `<nuttx/config.h>`. Therefore this
2845	creates the unresolved bridge symbol before the archive group is scanned, causing
2846	the earlier NuttX `libarch.a` to extract `bk7258_sdk_irq.o`. Extracting that one
2847	member also supplies unregister, set-priority, init, and deinit, so the later SDK
2848	`interrupt_base.c.obj` should remain unextracted. This avoids whole-archiving
2849	`libarch.a`, direct object-path duplication, or any official-tree/SDK edit.

## 2026-07-23 -- E08 root cause: correct inlined semantics, brittle immediate check

### Fresh object evidence

The exact fresh archive member was extracted from
`nuttx/staging/libarch.a(bk7258_sdk_irq.o)` and inspected with `nm -S -n` and
`objdump -dr`. The two static helpers were inlined, so they have no standalone
symbols. `bk_int_isr_register` contains the complete corrected decision:

```asm
cmp      r0, #27
ite      ne
movne.w  r8, #6
moveq.w  r8, #0
...
mov.w    r8, r8, lsl #5
...
bl       up_prioritize_irq
```

This is the intended compiled mapping:

```text
source == 27 -> logical 0 -> raw 0x00
source != 27 -> logical 6 -> shift left 5 -> raw 0xc0
```

The production correction is therefore present in the fresh object. No production
source change is required for this finding.

### Verifier defect

E08 currently requires `#27` plus a literal `#192`/`0xc0` in the register-symbol
disassembly. GCC instead retained logical constant `#6` and emitted a later
`lsl #5`; the raw value exists semantically but not as a literal immediate. E08 is
therefore a false negative caused by brittle constant-shape matching.

### Status and boundary

Production F1 semantics are object-confirmed, but Stage B remains `blocked` until
E08 is replaced with a predicate that recognizes the source-27 conditional 0/6
selection and priority-bit shift while still rejecting the historical uniform-6
object. No A1 invariant rerun, flash, board test, commit, or push occurred.

### Next single minimal action

Harden E08 around the compiled semantic sequence (`cmp #27`, conditional 6/0
selection, `lsl #5`, and the `up_prioritize_irq` relocation), then prove the new
predicate against both a stale/uniform-priority object and the fresh corrected
object before accepting 42/42 GREEN.

438	/****************************************************************************
439	 * Name: spin_lock_irqsave
440	 *
441	 * Description:
442	 *   If SMP is enabled:
443	 *     Disable local interrupts and take the lock spinlock and return
444	 *     the interrupt state.
445	 *
446	 *     NOTE: This API is very simple to protect data (e.g. H/W register
447	 *     or internal data structure) in SMP mode. But do not use this API
448	 *     with kernel APIs which suspend a caller thread. (e.g. nxsem_wait)
449	 *
450	 *   If SMP is not enabled:
451	 *     This function is equivalent to up_irq_save().
452	 *
453	 * Input Parameters:
454	 *   lock - Caller specific spinlock. not NULL.
455	 *
456	 * Returned Value:
457	 *   An opaque, architecture-specific value that represents the state of
458	 *   the interrupts prior to the call to spin_lock_irqsave(lock);
459	 *
460	 ****************************************************************************/
461	
462	#ifdef CONFIG_SPINLOCK
463	static inline_function
464	irqstate_t spin_lock_irqsave(FAR volatile spinlock_t *lock)
465	{
466	  irqstate_t flags;
467	
468	  /* Mark that we want to hold lock */
469	
470	  spinlock_mark_locking(&lock->info);
471	
472	  /* Notify that we are waiting for a spinlock */
473	
474	  sched_note_spinlock(lock, NOTE_SPINLOCK_LOCK);
475	
476	  /* If CONFIG_SCHED_CRITMONITOR_MAXTIME_BUSYWAIT >= 0, count busy-waiting. */
477	
478	  nxsched_critmon_busywait(true, return_address(0));
479	
480	  /* Lock without trace note */
481	
482	  flags = spin_lock_irqsave_notrace(lock);
483	
484	  /* Mark the spinlock has been locked */
485	
486	  spinlock_mark_locked(&lock->info);
487	
488	  /* Get the lock, end counting busy-waiting */
489	
490	  nxsched_critmon_busywait(false, return_address(0));
491	
492	  /* Notify that we have the spinlock */
493	
494	  sched_note_spinlock(lock, NOTE_SPINLOCK_LOCKED);
495	
496	  return flags;
497	}
498	#else
499	#  define spin_lock_irqsave(l) ((void)(l), up_irq_save())
500	#endif

concurrency defects. If no blocker survives, prepare (but do not flash) the
minimal user-only non-WDT SDK timer register/trigger/unregister/re-register test.

## 2026-07-23 -- Focused review finds lifecycle serialization defect F2

### Finding F2 (`Important`)

The callback dispatch path is nonblocking and the target NVIC line is disabled
during each individual lifecycle operation, but the complete bridge lifecycle is
not serialized. `bk_int_isr_register()`, `bk_int_isr_unregister()`,
`bk_int_set_priority()`, and `interrupt_deinit()` access the shared callback table
and NuttX IRQ ownership through multi-step sequences without a bridge-local
critical section/spinlock.

Concrete same-source replacement race on CPU0:

1. task/ISR A attaches the wrapper for handler A and is preempted before storing A;
2. task/ISR B completes replacement with handler B and enables the line;
3. A resumes, overwrites the callback with A and enables the line;
4. final state violates completion order: the later completed replacement B is
   lost even though both calls returned success.

A similar interleaving can make a concurrent custom-priority call lose to the
register path's default-priority write. `interrupt_deinit()` also reads the table
without serialization before calling unregister.

The current extracted object confirms there is no bridge-level PRIMASK save /
interrupt-disable / restore sequence in register, unregister, set-priority, or
deinit. The nested lock inside `irq_attach()` protects only `g_irqvector[]`; it
does not protect the bridge callback table or the complete lifecycle transaction.

### Required correction

Use a bridge-local `spinlock_t` with `spin_lock_irqsave()` /
`spin_unlock_irqrestore()` around complete lifecycle transactions. In the current
CPU0 configuration (`CONFIG_NCPUS=1`, no `CONFIG_SPINLOCK`) these APIs reduce to
`up_irq_save()` / `up_irq_restore()`, which prevents interrupt-driven preemption
without adding blocking work to dispatch. Keep dispatch lock-free. Use an internal
locked unregister helper so `interrupt_deinit()` can serialize its scan without
recursive locking.

### Status and boundary

Stage B returns to `blocked` pending F2. The prior 42/42 bridge and 18/18 A1 results
remain valid for their covered semantics but do not cover lifecycle serialization.
The current artifact must not be board-tested. No flash, board test, commit, or
push occurred.

### Next single minimal action

Add fail-closed source/object verifier gates for bridge-local lifecycle
serialization and demonstrate RED against the current artifact before changing
production bridge code.

## 2026-07-23 -- F2 object inspection proves production semantics; verifier is stale

### Internal helper

The fresh object contains a retained local symbol:

```text
bk7258_sdk_irq_unregister_locked: size 0x34
```

Its disassembly/relocations contain the complete teardown sequence:

```text
up_disable_irq
bk7258_clear_pending_irq
callback-table store of NULL
DSB / ISB
irq_attach (irq_detach expansion)
```

Both public register and unregister contain an
`R_ARM_THM_CALL bk7258_sdk_irq_unregister_locked` relocation. Register separately
retains wrapper `irq_attach`, `up_prioritize_irq`, callback publication/barriers,
and `up_enable_irq`.

### Lifecycle serialization shape

All four lifecycle paths contain the NuttX CPU0 IRQ-save implementation:

```text
mrs ..., BASEPRI
msr BASEPRI, 0x80-equivalent register
...
msr BASEPRI, saved register
```

This is the compiled form of `spin_lock_irqsave()` / restore in the current
Cortex-M33 configuration. The verifier incorrectly recognized only PRIMASK /
`cpsid` or external `up_irq_save` symbols. Register, unregister, custom priority,
and deinit all show the BASEPRI save/mask/restore sequence.

### Mapped-default shape after F2

Register still contains:

```text
cmp source, #27
movne logical_priority, #6
moveq logical_priority, #0
mov r1, logical_priority, lsl #5
bl up_prioritize_irq
```

E08 failed only because the shift is now fused into the move to argument `r1`,
rather than performed in place and then copied.

### Conclusion

The ten failures are verifier shape/call-graph defects introduced by the legitimate
internal-helper refactor; the fresh production object implements F1 and F2 as
intended. No production correction is required from this inspection.

42	class SymbolTables(object):
43	    def __init__(self, elffile, output):
44	        try:
45	            file = open(elffile, "rb")
46	            self.elffile = ELFFile(file)
47	        except FileNotFoundError:
48	            self.elffile = None
49	        self.output = output
50	        self.symbol_list = []
51	
52	    def symbol_filter(self, symbol):
53	        if symbol["st_info"]["type"] != "STT_FUNC":
54	            return None
55	        if symbol["st_info"]["bind"] == "STB_WEAK":
56	            return None
57	        if symbol["st_shndx"] == "SHN_UNDEF":
58	            return None
59	        return symbol
60	
61	    def print_symbol_tables(self, isnoconst=False):
62	        noconst = "const"
63	        if not isnoconst:
64	            noconst = ""
65	
66	        self.emitline("#include <nuttx/compiler.h>")
67	        self.emitline("#include <nuttx/symtab.h>\n")
68	        self.emitline("extern int g_nallsyms;\n")
69	        self.emitline(
70	            "extern struct symtab_s g_allsyms[%d + 2];\n" % len(self.symbol_list)
71	        )
72	        self.emitline("%s int g_nallsyms = %d + 2;" % (noconst, len(self.symbol_list)))
73	        self.emitline(
74	            "%s struct symtab_s g_allsyms[%d + 2] =\n{"
75	            % (noconst, len(self.symbol_list))
76	        )
77	        self.emitline('  { "Unknown", (FAR %s void *)0x00000000 },' % (noconst))
78	        for symbol in self.symbol_list:
79	            self.emitline(
80	                '  { "%s", (FAR %s void *)%s },' % (symbol[1], noconst, hex(symbol[0]))
81	            )
82	        self.emitline('  { "Unknown", (FAR %s void *)0xffffffff }\n};' % (noconst))
83	
84	    def get_symtable(self):
85	        symbol_tables = [
86	            (idx, s)
87	            for idx, s in enumerate(self.elffile.iter_sections())
88	            if isinstance(s, SymbolTableSection)
89	        ]
90	
91	        if not symbol_tables and self.elffile.num_sections() == 0:
92	            self.emitline("")
93	            return
94	
95	        for section_index, section in symbol_tables:
96	            if not isinstance(section, SymbolTableSection):
97	                continue
98	
99	            if section["sh_entsize"] == 0 or section.name != ".symtab":
100	                continue
101	
102	            return section
103	
104	    def parse_symbol(self, orderbyname=False):
105	        if self.elffile is None:
106	            return
107	        symtable = self.get_symtable()
108	        for nsym, symbol in enumerate(symtable.iter_symbols()):
109	            if self.symbol_filter(symbol) is not None:
110	                try:
111	                    symbol_name = cxxfilt.demangle(symbol.name)
112	                    func_name = re.sub(r"\(.*$", "", symbol_name)
113	                except cxxfilt.InvalidName:
114	                    symbol_name = symbol.name
115	                self.symbol_list.append((symbol["st_value"], func_name))
116	        if orderbyname:
117	            self.symbol_list = sorted(self.symbol_list, key=lambda item: item[1])
118	        else:
119	            self.symbol_list = sorted(self.symbol_list, key=lambda item: item[0])
120

122	        self.output.write(str(s) + "\n")

44	 *    - BK_OK: succeed
45	 *    - others: other errors.
46	 */

62	 *

66	 *

76	 *    - others: other errors.

9	# generic ARM common files), then add only the two BK7258-specific sources:
10	#
11	#   bk7258_vectors.c  - chip-provided Cortex-M vector table (66 entries),
12	#                       carrying the BK7236 app magic at slot 64/65 so it
13	#                       lands at image offset 0x100. Selected at Kconfig
14	#                       level via ARCH_HAVE_CUSTOM_VECTORS, which makes
15	#                       armv8-m -> arm_m drop arm_vectors.c automatically.
16	#
17	#   bk7258_start.c    - __start entry: mask IRQs, set VTOR, bare-write the
18	#                       "NUTTX N1" banner over UART1, spin. Stage N1 does
19	#                       NOT call nx_start().
20	############################################################################
21	
22	include armv8-m/Make.defs
23	
24	# Beken SDK include paths for the prebuilt library headers.
25	
26	INCLUDES += ${INCDIR_PREFIX}$(BOARD_DIR)$(DELIM)bk_idk$(DELIM)armino_as_lib$(DELIM)cp$(DELIM)include
27	INCLUDES += ${INCDIR_PREFIX}$(BOARD_DIR)$(DELIM)bk_idk$(DELIM)armino_as_lib$(DELIM)cp$(DELIM)config
28	
29	# Chip-specific sources (resolved via VPATH += $(CHIP_DIR) added by the
30	# arch Makefile, exactly like every other in-tree ARM chip).
31	#
32	# Stage N2 adds the full bring-up set on top of the N1 vector/start pair:
33	#   bk7258_lowputc.c     polled arm_lowputc()/up_putc() over UART1
34	#   bk7258_serial.c      poll-based uart_ops_s console lower-half
35	#   bk7258_irq.c         NVIC up_*irq*() glue
36	#   bk7258_timerisr.c    SysTick up_timer_initialize()
37	#   bk7258_allocateheap.c up_allocate_heap()
38	
39	CHIP_CSRCS  = bk7258_vectors.c
40	CHIP_CSRCS += bk7258_start.c
41	CHIP_CSRCS += bk7258_lowputc.c
42	CHIP_CSRCS += bk7258_serial.c
43	CHIP_CSRCS += bk7258_irq.c
44	CHIP_CSRCS += bk7258_timerisr.c
45	CHIP_CSRCS += bk7258_allocateheap.c
46	CHIP_CSRCS += bk7258_os_adapt.c
47	CHIP_CSRCS += bk7258_sdk_stubs.c
48	
49	# Stage B: replace the SDK private CM33 callback table with NuttX irq_attach()
50	# ownership for SDK interrupt sources 0..63.  Default off outside the Stage B
51	# branch so the A1 board-verified baseline remains selectable.
52	
53	ifeq ($(CONFIG_BK7258_SDK_IRQ_BRIDGE),y)
54	CHIP_CSRCS += bk7258_sdk_irq.c
55	endif
56	
57	# Stage N5-D6-A: on-chip flash data-partition MTD (read-only path).  Gated on
58	# CONFIG_BK7258_FLASH_MTD; default off so normal firmware is unchanged.
59	
60	ifeq ($(CONFIG_BK7258_FLASH_MTD),y)
61	CHIP_CSRCS += bk7258_flash_mtd.c
62	endif
63	
64	# Stage N4-D1: deterministic 320 MHz CPU0 clock bring-up.
65	
66	ifeq ($(CONFIG_BK7258_CLOCK_320M),y)
67	CHIP_CSRCS += bk7258_clock.c
68	endif
69	
70	# Compile the common Cortex-M SysTick lower half (arm_systick.c, which
71	# provides systick_initialize() used by bk7258_timerisr.c).  The shared
72	# arm_m/Make.defs gates this on CONFIG_ARM_M_SYSTICK, a symbol no Kconfig
73	# ever defines (a latent typo -- the real symbol is CONFIG_ARM_SYSTICK,
74	# which CONFIG_ARMV8M_SYSTICK selects).  VPATH already lists arm_m/, so
75	# referencing the file by basename resolves to arch/arm/src/arm_m/arm_systick.c
76	# without touching the upstream tree.
77	
78	ifeq ($(CONFIG_ARM_SYSTICK),y)
79	CHIP_CSRCS += arm_systick.c
80	endif
81	
82	# Stage N4-D2: the BK7258 DVFS lower half.  Selected by BK7258_CLOCK_320M
83	# (boot-time bringup) and reachable standalone via /proc/dvfs when
84	# BK7258_DVFS_PROCFS is on.  bk7258_clk_ll.h is consumed inline by both
85	# bk7258_clock.c and bk7258_dvfs.c; no separate .c for it.
86	
87	ifeq ($(CONFIG_BK7258_DVFS),y)
88	CHIP_CSRCS += bk7258_dvfs.c
89	endif
90	
91	ifeq ($(CONFIG_BK7258_DVFS_PROCFS),y)
92	CHIP_CSRCS += bk7258_dvfs_procfs.c
93	endif
94	
95	# Force the link entry point to our __start (defined in bk7258_start.c).
96	# --build-id=none keeps the image deterministic and avoids leaking any
97	# build-id bytes that could shift the offset of later sections.
98	
99	# Stage B2: APB watchdog lower-half driver.  Takes over the bootloader's WDT
100	# after boot and registers /dev/watchdog0.  Default y.
101	
102	ifeq ($(CONFIG_BK7258_WDT),y)
103	CHIP_CSRCS += bk7258_wdt.c
104	endif
105	
106	# Disable FreeRTOS assumptions in SDK headers (reference: 7236N Make.defs:110-120)
107	CFLAGS += -DCONFIG_FREERTOS=0 -DCONFIG_FREERTOS_SMP=0
108	# NuttX automonitor owns watchdog keepalive; the wrapper stops SDK TIMER_ID2.
109	CFLAGS += -DCONFIG_INT_WDT=0 -DCONFIG_TASK_WDT=0 -DCONFIG_INT_AON_WDT=0
110	CFLAGS += -DCONFIG_SYSTEM_CTRL=1 -DCONFIG_NMI_WDT_EN=1
111	CFLAGS += -DCONFIG_DEBUG_VERSION=0 -DCONFIG_GPIO_RETENTION_SUPPORT=0
112	CFLAGS += -DCONFIG_AON_RTC=0 -DCONFIG_AON_RTC_64BIT=0
113	CFLAGS += -DCONFIG_SOC_BK7256XX=0 -DCONFIG_SOC_BK7236XX=0 -DCONFIG_SOC_BK7239XX=0
114	
115	LDFLAGS += --build-id=none --entry=__start

## 2026-07-23 -- Timer-test channel and manual-command design fixed

### Timer channel selection

The localized CP SDK configuration disproves the earlier TIMER4/TIMER5 candidate:

```text
CONFIG_TIMER_SUPPORT_ID_BITS = 7  -> only TIMER_ID0..2 are accepted
CONFIG_TIMER_US = 1               -> TIMER_ID0 is reserved for the us timer
SDK timer API warning             -> TIMER_ID2 is used for time calibration
```

`bk_timer_start()` rejects IDs 3..5 through
`TIMER_RETURN_TIMER_ID_IS_ERR()`. A bounded source search found TIMER_ID1 users only
in the optional touch demo/driver, and none of the touch timer callbacks/entry points
are retained in the current final ELF. Therefore the test candidate is:

```text
SDK timer channel : TIMER_ID1
SDK IRQ source    : INT_SRC_TIMER (source 3)
NuttX logical IRQ : 19
status bit        : BIT(TIMER_ID1) = 0x2
```

The command will fail closed at runtime unless `bk_timer_get_enable_status()` reports
all six timer channels idle. This is stricter than checking group 0 alone because the
exported `timer_clear_isr_status()` reads and clears the six-bit status word for both
timer groups.

### Restoration and integration design

`bk_timer_driver_deinit()` is not a safe restoration primitive: it stops and resets
all six channels and does not unregister the two top-level IRQ sources. The test will
instead add a test-gated, lock-protected snapshot helper to the overlay bridge, save
the existing `INT_SRC_TIMER` callback, and restore it through the normal
`bk_int_isr_register()` path on every exit.

The test remains manual and non-booting:

- a gated chip-local runner owns SDK headers, timer status acknowledgement, callback
  counters, cleanup, and saved-handler restoration;
- the linked contest app contributes only a small NSH built-in wrapper named
  `bkirqtest`;
- the gate selects NSH built-in-app support, but no bring-up path invokes the test;
- TIMER_ID1 starts only after the all-channel-idle guard passes.

Planned live sequence:

```text
snapshot original INT_SRC_TIMER owner
register callback A -> start TIMER1 -> require callback/status bit
unregister source -> start TIMER1 -> require hardware status but unchanged counters
register callback B -> start TIMER1 -> require callback/status bit
stop/clear TIMER1 -> restore original owner
```

### Status and boundary

This is a source-backed design result only. The timer test has not yet been
implemented or built. The existing F2 artifact remains `build-verified` (bridge
48/48, A1 invariants 18/18) and not `board-verified`. No flash, board test, commit,
or push occurred.

### Next single minimal action

Implement the gated bridge snapshot helper, chip-local TIMER1 test runner, and manual
`bkirqtest` wrapper; then update this worklog before the first build.

Another Claude session sent a message:
<teammate-message teammate_id="timer-conflict-scout" color="purple" summary="Timer 5 looks safest">
Bounded read-only timer-channel investigation complete.

Recommendation
- Best manual Stage B non-WDT channel: use `TIMER_ID5` and register the SDK callback on `INT_SRC_TIMER1`.
- `TIMER_ID4` also looks free in the current artifact, but `TIMER_ID5` is the safest pick because the SDK header explicitly calls out `TIMER_ID2` and `TIMER_ID3` as special/reserved, while I found no current build/overlay use of `TIMER_ID5`.
- Bridge-side mapped NuttX IRQ would be `16 + 13 = 29` if you need the concrete line (`INT_SRC_TIMER1` is source 13).

Evidence
1. Current generated config uses the bridge and WDT, but watchdog automonitor is not timer-based.
- `/home/lijian/project/open-vela/nuttx/.config:221-229` shows `CONFIG_ARCH_CHIP_BK7258=y`, `CONFIG_BK7258_WDT=y`, `CONFIG_BK7258_SDK_IRQ_BRIDGE=y`.
- `/home/lijian/project/open-vela/nuttx/.config:558-570` shows `CONFIG_TIMER=y`, `CONFIG_TIMER_ARCH=y`, `CONFIG_WATCHDOG_AUTOMONITOR=y`, `CONFIG_WATCHDOG_AUTOMONITOR_BY_WDOG=y`, and `CONFIG_WATCHDOG_AUTOMONITOR_BY_TIMER` is not set.
- Board defconfig matches that shape at `/home/lijian/project/open-vela/contest2026_135_yongwangzhiqian/board/bk7258_t5ai/configs/nsh/defconfig:39-43`.

2. NuttX system tick does not consume BK SDK timer channels.
- `/home/lijian/project/open-vela/contest2026_135_yongwangzhiqian/board/bk7258_t5ai/chip/bk7258_timerisr.c:79-109` shows `up_timer_initialize()` programming SysTick and calling `systick_initialize(true, cpu_hz, -1)`; lines `104-109` state `minor=-1` means no `/dev/timerN` node and that this timer is the dedicated system clock only.

3. The only confirmed live BK SDK timer use in the current build is the SDK WDT feeder on `TIMER_ID2`.
- `/home/lijian/project/open-vela/contest2026_135_yongwangzhiqian/board/bk7258_t5ai/chip/bk7258_wdt.h:8-16` documents the vendor WDT path: `bk_wdt_driver_init -> bk_timer_start(TIMER_ID2, 1s, feed_handle)`.
- `/home/lijian/project/open-vela/contest2026_135_yongwangzhiqian/board/bk7258_t5ai/chip/bk7258_wdt.c:222-232` initializes the SDK timer driver/WDT state and immediately calls `bk_timer_stop(TIMER_ID2)` so NuttX automonitor owns keepalive.
- `/home/lijian/project/open-vela/nuttx/nuttx.map:827-834` shows `libdriver.a(timer_driver.c.obj)` is pulled in via `bk7258_wdt.o` for `bk_timer_driver_init`, and WDT-related SDK objects are pulled by the same path.
- Linked-image disassembly of `/home/lijian/project/open-vela/nuttx/nuttx`, symbol `bk_wdt_driver_init` at `0x0202a744`, shows `movs r0,#2; mov.w r1,#1000; ldr r2,=bk_wdt_feed_handle; bl bk_timer_start`, i.e. WDT init really starts `TIMER_ID2`.

4. BK7258 SDK timer topology is 6 channels split into 2 interrupt groups of 3.
- `/home/lijian/project/open-vela/contest2026_135_yongwangzhiqian/board/bk7258_t5ai/bk_idk/armino_as_lib/cp/include/driver/hal/hal_timer_types.h:43-51` defines `TIMER_ID0..TIMER_ID5`.
- `/home/lijian/project/open-vela/contest2026_135_yongwangzhiqian/board/bk7258_t5ai/bk_idk/armino_as_lib/cp/include/soc/bk7258/timer_cap.h:21-25` says 6 channels, 2 groups, 3 channels/group.
- `/home/lijian/project/open-vela/contest2026_135_yongwangzhiqian/board/bk7258_t5ai/bk_idk/armino_as_lib/cp/include/driver/timer.h:63-65` contains the vendor note: `timer2 has been used for time cali`, `timer3 has been used for clock`.

5. Group-to-interrupt mapping in the linked artifact is explicit.
- `/home/lijian/project/open-vela/contest2026_135_yongwangzhiqian/board/bk7258_t5ai/bk_idk/armino_as_lib/cp/include/driver/int_types.h:98-113` defines `INT_SRC_TIMER = 3` and `INT_SRC_TIMER1 = 13` for this SoC family branch.
- Linked-image disassembly of `/home/lijian/project/open-vela/nuttx/nuttx`, symbol `bk_timer_driver_init` at `0x0202a4d8`, shows two registrations:
  - `r0 = 3`, callback `0x02034891` -> `bk_int_isr_register(INT_SRC_TIMER, timer_isr, NULL)`
  - `r0 = 13`, callback `0x02034865` -> `bk_int_isr_register(INT_SRC_TIMER1, timer1_isr, NULL)`
- Linked-image disassembly then shows:
  - `timer_isr` at `0x02034890` loops `r4 = 0 .. 2`
  - `timer1_isr` at `0x02034864` loops `r4 = 3 .. 5`
  So `TIMER_ID4` and `TIMER_ID5` both dispatch through `INT_SRC_TIMER1`, while `TIMER_ID0..2` dispatch through `INT_SRC_TIMER`.

6. Bridge mapping for the board test.
- `/home/lijian/project/open-vela/contest2026_135_yongwangzhiqian/board/bk7258_t5ai/chip/bk7258_sdk_irq.h:24-29` defines the bridge source range and priorities.
- `/home/lijian/project/open-vela/contest2026_135_yongwangzhiqian/board/bk7258_t5ai/chip/bk7258_sdk_irq.c:68-78` maps SDK source `n` to NuttX IRQ `BK7258_SDK_IRQ_FIRST + n`; the compile-time assertion at `:44-45` states source `0..63` maps to IRQ `16..79`. Therefore `INT_SRC_TIMER1` (13) maps to IRQ 29.

Implement the gated bridge snapshot helper, chip-local TIMER1 test runner, and manual
`bkirqtest` wrapper; then update this worklog before the first build.

## 2026-07-23 -- Manual TIMER1 bridge test implemented (unbuilt)

### Source/config implementation

The default-off `CONFIG_BK7258_SDK_IRQ_TIMER_TEST` gate now depends on the production
bridge plus NSH and selects NuttX built-in-app support. The BK7258 NSH defconfig
explicitly enables the gate.

New/updated implementation layers:

- `bk7258_sdk_irq.c/.h`: test-gated, bridge-lock-protected handler snapshot; it reads
  the current callback without changing NVIC/NuttX ownership, while normal dispatch
  remains lock-free;
- `bk7258_sdk_irq_timer_test.c`: chip-local SDK-aware runner, selected in both classic
  Make and CMake only under the test gate;
- `board.h`: exposes only the runner entry to the app layer;
- `app/hello_app/bk7258_sdk_irq_test_main.c`: thin manual built-in wrapper named
  `bkirqtest`; existing `hello_app` remains selectable and no bring-up path calls the
  test;
- app Make/CMake integration supports both commands without exposing private SDK
  headers to the app target.

### Fail-closed runtime sequence

The runner compile-time pins TIMER_ID1/source 3 and verifies that the pinned SDK
support mask includes TIMER1. At runtime it:

1. rejects concurrent command invocation;
2. snapshots and requires the existing `INT_SRC_TIMER` owner;
3. refuses to run unless all six SDK timer enable bits are zero;
4. stops/clears TIMER1, installs callback A, triggers the 50 ms hardware timer, and
   requires status bit `0x2` plus an A count;
5. unregisters source 3, triggers TIMER1 again, and requires status bit `0x2` while
   both callback counters remain unchanged;
6. installs callback B, triggers again, and requires B/status while A stays unchanged;
7. on every path after ownership is touched, stops/clears TIMER1 and restores the
   saved SDK owner through `bk_int_isr_register()`.

ISR callbacks only acknowledge status and update volatile counters. They do not log,
allocate, block, or call watchdog APIs. The test does not use
`bk_timer_driver_deinit()`.

### Status and boundary

Implementation is complete in source but is **unbuilt and unverified**. The only
verified firmware remains the earlier F2 compile/static artifact. No build, flash,
board test, commit, or push occurred for this timer-test change.

### Next single minimal action

Review the exact new source/config diff, run whitespace/config prechecks, then perform
the authorized fresh distclean/build and static verification. Do not flash.

## 2026-07-23 -- Missing-command root cause isolated to package category traversal

### Exact split

The chip side is correct: `libarch.a` contains `bk7258_sdk_irq_timer_test.o`, and the
archive exports the runner, both callbacks, and the bridge snapshot helper. They are
removed from the final ELF only because no app references the runner.

The app side is never traversed. Root `packages/Make.defs` includes only:

```make
include $(wildcard $(APPDIR)/packages/*/Make.defs)
```

The manifest links the team app at
`packages/demos/contest2026_135_hello_app`, but `packages/demos/Make.defs` does not
exist. Therefore the root wildcard never reaches the app's own `Make.defs`; no app
object or built-in registration is generated.

### Fix boundary

Do not edit the official `packages/` checkout. Add team-owned `packages/demos`
category aggregators through new manifest `linkfile` entries, so classic Make reaches
child `Make.defs` and the CMake/Kconfig backends have equivalent category traversal.
Then apply the manifest links locally and rebuild.

### Status and next action

Timer test remains post-build RED and not board-testable. No flash, commit, or push
occurred. Next: add the team-owned category aggregators + manifest links, refresh
linkfiles locally, and rebuild once.
